runners_data.name: Ataturk

races.paceDynamic: Joulany, Alfaraz, and My Love Is King will engage in a genuine pace battle from the start, creating a strong gallop over this stamina-testing 1m2f trip. The quartet of prominent racers (Maltese Cross, Shabab Al Ahli, Sahara King, Barrister) will create significant congestion behind the leaders, particularly dangerous turning for home. With only two hold-up horses in the field and genuine pace pressure guaranteed, this race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace without getting caught in traffic. The strong gallop will expose stamina limitations and set up tactical speed for those positioned just off the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners (Joulany, Alfaraz, My Love Is King) go too fast early and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find them out over this demanding trip, allowing the prominent runners with tactical speed to surge past. Those who tracked the pace without getting involved in the early battle will have the perfect stalking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three leaders (most likely Joulany given his breeding) can dictate terms and kick clear
scenarios.body: The pace will still be strong enough to set up the race, but the winner will come from the front rank rather than behind. Class and stamina will prevail over pure tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Congestion Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners get tangled up behind the leaders turning for home
scenarios.body: Traffic problems will compromise several fancied runners, allowing either a leader to steal it or a hold-up horse to come through late. The pace will be genuine enough to bring stamina into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unraced Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If either Easwrith Destiny or Much brings significantly more ability than their OR suggests
scenarios.body: The strong pace and stamina test will suit a well-bred newcomer with untapped potential over this trip. Their clean run from the back could prove decisive if the pace is as strong as predicted.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems with Maltese Cross, Shabab Al Ahli, Sahara King and Barrister all wanting the same prominent position behind three confirmed leaders
Monitor the early pace battle between Joulany, Alfaraz and My Love Is King as whoever gets the easiest time could dictate the outcome
Keep an eye on the unraced pair Easwrith Destiny and Much as their hold-up styles could benefit from a pace collapse
Watch for any market moves on the Appleby newcomer Shabab Al Ahli given the stable's excellent record with lightly-raced horses
Monitor how the 160+ day absences affect Sahara King, My Love Is King and Joulany as fitness could be crucial over this demanding trip

races.name: cityam.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Proven front-running winner under Paetel who excels when dictating pace, 20 days since last run ideal for peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Always behind at Kempton three weeks ago but should be benefited from that run
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f winner from the front (under Mason Paetel) at Newmarket last May who also scored with a prominent ride over hurdles at Cheltenham (2m5f) in November; had a bit to prove on AW (and over 2m on Flat) when always behind at Kempton three weeks ago but should be benefited from that run.

runners_data.name: Maxident
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader but 220-day layoff is a concern despite David Egan's booking and recent trainer form

runners_data.name: Classical Allusion
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs pace to aim at, Constitution Hill form looks strong but lacks experience
runners_data.comment: Won debut; kept superstar hurdler Constitution Hill up to his work at Kempton (1m4f, AW)
runners_data.spotlight: Won Southwell maiden (1m4f, AW) in September on debut; second favourite to superstar hurdler Constitution Hill in Kempton novice (1m4f, AW) last month and chased him home 2l adrift, perhaps giving him more to think about than had widely been expected; not easy to pin down but 2m is plausible and his connections presumably like the look of his opening handicap mark.

runners_data.name: Call My Bluff
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 44-day break, second in this race previously but 758-day absence before recent comeback
runners_data.comment: Major questions to answer regarding the ground and what he's currently capable of
runners_data.spotlight: 5-25; second in this race in 2023 and close third in the Chester Cup (2m2f, again on soft; favourite off 9lb higher than today) that May but absent for 758 days afterwards; while not disgraced on reappearance last October, he then tailed off on AW last month; major questions to answer regarding the ground and what he's currently capable of.

runners_data.name: Blazeon Five
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer carrying top weight, 91 days since last run and prefers softer ground than today's good
runners_data.comment: Ended last year in storming form trick and not disgraced in January latest; not dismissed

runners_data.name: Pole Star

runners_data.name: Caprelo

runners_data.comment: Peak efforts on last two AW starts; chance on that but needs to improve his turf form
runners_data.spotlight: Probably acts on any going but peak efforts were on AW at Kempton (2m) where he won in September and was runner-up in December; chance on that but needs to improve his turf form.

runners_data.name: Francesco Baracca
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner best on AW surfaces, 14-day turnaround quick after disappointing Lingfield effort

runners_data.spotlight: Has done best on AW, including three wins at Wolverhampton (1m6f/2m) in the last six months; well held at Lingfield two weeks ago but has a modest record there; has won twice on turf, latterly on good ground at Bath (1m6f) last June but none of his turf form matches today's mark.

races.paceDynamic: Maxident is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will dictate terms from flag to finish over 2m½f. With Lavender Hill Mob and Call My Bluff likely pressing but not challenging early, Maxident should get uncontested fractions through the opening mile. The majority of this field - Classical Allusion, Blazeon Five, Pole Star, Caprelo and Francesco Baracca - are hold-up performers who will need the pace to develop. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the moderate pace and kick when it quickens, rather than hold-up horses facing a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Maxident gets soft fractions and stays strong
scenarios.body: The confirmed front runner faces no early pressure and can control the race to suit his stamina, with the hold-up brigade left with too much to do when the pace finally lifts. Maxident's 220-day break becomes less relevant if he can dictate throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Lavender Hill Mob or Call My Bluff press Maxident early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more honest through the middle stages, setting up perfectly for the proven front-running winner Lavender Hill Mob to strike or Call My Bluff to repeat his 2023 second. This creates the right tempo for horses who race prominently rather than from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The tactical nature plays into the hands of a classy hold-up performer like Classical Allusion or the returning Pole Star who can quicken off a crawling pace. The lack of early pace becomes an advantage for horses with a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If genuine pace develops throughout and it becomes a true staying test
scenarios.body: The 2m½f trip and sustained gallop sorts out the genuine stayers from the rest, potentially suiting Blazeon Five's hat-trick form or Francesco Baracca's recent AW distance wins. Late pace favours horses proven over the trip.

watchPoints.text: Maxident's 220-day layoff could see him weaken dramatically in the final half-mile despite controlling early
Classical Allusion lacks race experience with only two career starts and may not handle race pressure
Lavender Hill Mob's front-running style under Paetel could press Maxident into honest fractions early
Blazeon Five carries top weight of 132lbs which may prove decisive over 2m½f on good ground
Call My Bluff showed he retains ability on comeback but needs to prove 44-day gap brings improvement

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Full Of Surprises Handicap

runners_data.name: Fort Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with proven class advantage and William Buick's tactical expertise after 163-day break
runners_data.comment: 2-2 on Kempton AW (7f), winning narrowly on both starts; should have plenty more to give
runners_data.spotlight: Had a nose to spare when making a winning debut last October (7f, AW) and won by a head back at Kempton three weeks later; it's hard to knock his attitude and this unbeaten colt commands plenty of respect on his seasonal, handicap and turf debut.

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form after runaway AW win, perfectly suited to this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Heavily backed and won by wide margin at Southwell 12 days ago; 6lb well in under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Fairly useful form as a 2yo, including winning debut, but took his form to a new level with a runaway success at Southwell (7f, AW) on return 12 days ago; this is a stronger race but he is 6lb well in under the penalty and the money that came for him at Southwell strongly suggested he was thought to be smart; stall 1 is a potential query but lots to like otherwise.

runners_data.name: Stellar Sunrise
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 7f form but 174-day absence creates fitness doubt
runners_data.comment: Below par in Gr 3 on soft when last seen but improving rapidly beforehand; may do better
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt as a 2yo when seeing off 14 rivals at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good); improved for the step up to 7f when impressing in an 18-runner nursery at York's Ebor meeting (good to firm); only 5-1 for a Group 3 over C&D when last seen in October but he dropped away late on soft ground that may not have been ideal; could still have more to offer back on a sounder surface.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Steps
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 237-day layoff with trainer form concerns
runners_data.comment: 6f win here on debut; came up short in stronger company afterwards; returns in warm race
runners_data.spotlight: Ready winner of a 6f fillies' maiden here on debut last July; came up short in stronger company in three subsequent runs (5f-7f); absent for 237 days and she returns in a warm handicap; stable also runs Tamashal.

runners_data.name: Shaman Champion
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching to Clive Cox after 210-day break, zero stable winners recently
runners_data.comment: Pretty useful as 2yo, including C&D; sold 160,000gns since latest; personal best required
runners_data.spotlight: Easy win on his debut (5f, good to firm) and showed fairly useful ability in five subsequent starts for Richard Hughes, including a C&D second when last seen in September (solid form); sold for 160,000gns the following month; begins this campaign up another 3lb; big personal best is required on his first run for a trainer who won this race in 2022 and 2023.

runners_data.name: Crown Office
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with class edge but long absence and Haggas 2/26 recent record concern
runners_data.comment: 6f maiden winner as a 2yo; brings untapped potential to this handicap debut; strong claims
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising debut at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; strong form) last August; plenty went wrong at York on his second start and he showed his true colours when comfortably on top at the finish at Leicester when last seen in October; appeared to win that race in spite of the drop back to 6f and soft ground and he brings considerable potential to this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Caballo Grande
runners_data.note: Natural leader with weak AW form but suited to making the running
runners_data.comment: Easy AW wins from the front (6f-7f) on last two starts; this looks a much stiffer test
runners_data.spotlight: Inexperience evident on his 2yo debut (6f, good) and he has since made all for easy AW wins at Southwell (6f) and Wolverhampton (7f); the form of neither of those wins looks especially strong but he was in a different class to his rivals; this will be a far stiffer test of his credentials.

runners_data.name: May Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Group race experience but long absence after disappointing efforts
runners_data.comment: Easy 7f AW win last summer before down the field in two Group 3s; wind/gelding ops since
runners_data.spotlight: Ready winner of a 7f novice at Southwell on his second start; came up short in two Group 3 events afterwards (tried in a hood on second occasion); he has since undergone wind and gelding operations; hard pressed to describe him as well handicapped on what we have seen but the surgeries could unlock more.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who found best form at 7f+ with strong finishing kick
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over 7f+; gelded since winning York sales race in October; interesting on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Had become exposed over sprint trips but his form took off when upped to 7f+ on his final two runs as a 2yo, following his Ffos Las maiden win with a last-ditch success in a York sales race in October; gelded since; making his handicap debut on his eighth start but he looks on an appealing mark.

runners_data.name: Amorim
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 210-day break with solid 6f form translating up
runners_data.comment: Promise over 6f as a 2yo; gelded since last seen; improvement required for the new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Raced over 6f as a 2yo, winning a Windsor novice by daylight last June and third in Listed race here three weeks later; soft ground excuses his poor run when last seen; improvement required for the longer trip and/or a gelding operation if he is to win today.

runners_data.name: Tamashal
runners_data.note: Improving front-runner in career-best form with recent course winner form
runners_data.comment: Improving run by run; into a stronger race for his turf debut, so needs to progress again
runners_data.spotlight: Major eyecatcher on debut and he has improved with each subsequent run, winning a 1m maiden at Chelmsford and following up in a 7f handicap at Southwell three weeks ago; up 3lb against stronger opposition this time.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent Southwell form and 5lb claimer reducing weight
runners_data.comment: Two good runs for his new yard but this looks a much tougher assignment
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice for Jack Channon; successful stable debut at Southwell last month and ran another solid race when third behind two reopposing rivals at Southwell three weeks ago; this race is tougher.

runners_data.name: Peel Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up type requiring significant improvement after gelding operation
runners_data.comment: 6f maiden win was followed by two nursery defeats; improvement required after a gelding op
runners_data.spotlight: 6f maiden win last summer; unplaced in good nurseries at York and Doncaster when last seen; gelded during his absence; needs to raise his game.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Scholar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form but facing stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: Ended 2025 on a roll and ran well on his return; this looks tougher though
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 in fine form, completing a hat-trick when powering through the mud at Doncaster in November (6f); promising second behind Tamashal at Southwell on return three weeks ago; in deeper waters today.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Prominent performer transformed since gelding with back-to-back wins this month
runners_data.comment: Two bloodless handicap wins this month; 6lb well in but taking on much stiffer opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after his three 2yo runs and proved a different proposition in two handicap runs this month, running away with a Class 5 at Southwell (1m) two weeks ago and following up at Wolverhampton (7f; Class 6) eight days ago; 6lb well in under his penalty but he is taking on a much higher calibre of opponent this afternoon.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo Grande and Tamashal will set a genuine pace from the gates, with both confirmed front-runners having led in recent victories. The presence of two natural leaders creates an honest gallop but not an overly fierce one, as neither jockey will want to commit too early in this 15-runner handicap. Several prominent racers including Fort Rock, Stellar Sunrise and Amorim will track the leaders closely, setting up a tactical battle from 3f out. This honest pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish late, particularly those with proven finishing kicks like Colori Forever, Crown Office and Astrazar.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not fierce between Caballo Grande and Tamashal
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop sets up perfectly for closers with finishing speed to sweep up late. Strong stayers with tactical speed will find gaps in the final furlong as the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Fort Rock and Stellar Sunrise can secure ideal tracking positions behind the leaders
scenarios.body: These class performers avoid the early battle but stay close enough to strike when the pace lifts. Their proven ability at this trip gives them the edge over pure front-runners and hold-up types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo Grande or Tamashal can steal a march while the other over-races
scenarios.body: One leader gets first run while the other fights for position, allowing the smarter tactical ride to stay clear. Recent AW form translates well to this good turf surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and completely collapse
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace becomes a sprint finish where any horse with a turn of foot can win. This benefits any runner who gets a clean run regardless of normal running style.

watchPoints.text: Caballo Grande and Tamashal must avoid going too fast early as both are natural leaders meeting for first time
Fort Rock and Stellar Sunrise carry fitness concerns after lengthy absences despite having class edge
Colori Forever's hold-up style perfectly matches the likely pace shape after impressive recent win
Several trainers including Clive Cox (0/10) and Richard Hannon (6/47) show poor recent strike rates
On The Inlet has been transformed since gelding with two wins this month and rising confidence

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Handicap

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 185-day break with strong course form and ideal tactical setup

runners_data.name: Change Sings
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form who was second in this race last year off higher mark
runners_data.comment: 2nd in this race last year and 2lb lower today; solid 3rd at Kempton on return; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Getting on for two years since his last win but he was a good second in this race last year (off 2lb higher mark) and he returned to action with a promising third at Kempton three weeks ago; solid contender.

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Classy hold-up horse returning from Portland disappointment but has winning form at this trip
runners_data.comment: 3-6 and open to further progress this year; gelded; stall 1 is perhaps not ideal today
runners_data.spotlight: Managed only a midfield finish in the Portland Handicap (5.6f, good) when last seen in September but he was favourite for that prestigious event having won well at Newmarket on penultimate start; still has potential after just six starts, three of which have resulted in 6f wins; looks the type to be contesting major sprint handicaps this summer but stall 1 is a slight query on his return (best pace looks middle to high); gelded since last seen.

runners_data.name: Gweedore
runners_data.note: Prominent 9yo veteran stepping back to 6f for first time with mixed results at this distance
runners_data.comment: Grand old servant but this is not sure to be the day he registers his first 6f success
runners_data.spotlight: He has been a fine advertisement for Katie Scott, winning 13 races over 7f and 1m; 0-6 at this trip but he was beaten less than one length in the 2023 Ayr Gold Cup; recent Musselburgh return should have blown away the cobwebs but others are still more appealing for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Lakers
runners_data.note: Prominent type in decent form but kicked before start last time which explains poor run
runners_data.comment: Below par on Good Friday (kicked before start) but progressive over this trip beforehand
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed at 6f; this mark is in range judged on his two placed efforts this winter; failed to fire on Good Friday but he received a kick before the start which won't have helped; no surprise to see him bounce back.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner who will get uncontested lead and sustainable fractions
runners_data.comment: Progressive on AW in late 2025; it's interesting that he makes his handicap debut here
runners_data.spotlight: 320,000euros yearling but didn't reach the track for Godolphin and sold for 16,000gns in January 2025; three promising runs on AW in late 2025, second at Wolverhampton and Newcastle (both 5f) before justifying odds-on favouritism at Newcastle when upped to 6f in November; could have been found easier opportunities for his handicap debut and this is his trainer's first runner at Newbury; those factors both heighten interest in this unexposed 4yo.

runners_data.name: Brian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling recently but fair mark and Newbury suits his style
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on last three starts but goes well here and Tom Marquand is a notable booking
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy defeats on his last three starts, including his Kempton reappearance three weeks ago; he's on a fair mark on the pick of his efforts though and this track does seem to suit him well; Tom Marquand is a notable booking for the stable (his nine rides for Stan Moore have yielded two wins, a second, three thirds and two fourths); lively outsider.

runners_data.name: Photosynthesis
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won 6f handicap here last year but disappointing on return
runners_data.comment: Third in this race last year; needs to bounce back from a poor run at Newcastle in January
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing at Newcastle in January; had earlier dug deep to win a Newmarket handicap (6f, good) on his final 4yo outing; third in this race 12 months ago and can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Mirabeau
runners_data.note: Hold-up type dropping back to 6f for first time since 2yo debut after longer distance campaign
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark if the drop back to sprinting works the oracle; Oisin Murphy booked
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned over as far as 10.3f and this will be his first 6f run since his 2yo debut; well beaten in the Lincoln on his reappearance (1m, good to soft); dangerous mark judged on best 2025 effort (7f, good to soft); trip is a query but Oisin Murphy a notable booking.

runners_data.name: Juan Les Pins
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist in red-hot form with recent 6f win, low weight advantage
runners_data.comment: Unpenalised for last week's Thirsk win (6f, good) but this is a big step up in class
runners_data.spotlight: He had dropped a long way in the weights prior to popping up at Newcastle (5f) last month; ran well at Doncaster ten days later and back on the scoresheet with a Thirsk win last week (6f, good); won that apprentice race (no penalty today) last time with more authority than the winning margin might suggest but he is up in class today.

runners_data.name: Cindy Lou Who
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent 2024 form but stepping up significantly in class
runners_data.comment: Progressive last year and reappearance Listed 2nd was better; 15lb well in; obvious claims
runners_data.spotlight: Made giant strides for Tony Carroll last season, winning four times (three of them at Bath); confirmed her affinity for Bath, as well as the fact that she had done well over the winter, when short-headed in a Bath Listed race on Easter Sunday (5f, good); 15lb well in on this return to handicap company; obvious chance.

runners_data.name: Wheels Of Fire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form after gelding operation with recent Musselburgh win
runners_data.comment: Easy 5f win two weeks ago (soft ground); 8lb rise demands another personal best
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after his 3yo campaign; down the field at Newcastle on return but much more like it when skipping clear in the closing stages at Musselburgh 13 days ago (5f, soft; edged left under pressure); return to 6f no problem but an 8lb rise in the weights might be.

runners_data.name: Hucklesbrook
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 121-day break, won useful handicaps as 3yo
runners_data.comment: Won two good 6f handicaps last summer; quiet since; not solid back from four months off
runners_data.spotlight: Won a couple of useful 6f 3yo handicaps in the first half of 2025; no progress since but he is edging back down the weights; returns from four months off and he will need to be at his best.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with 6f course wins but offered little on 5f return last time
runners_data.comment: Two 6f wins last summer; low-key return at Newcastle last month; others look safer
runners_data.spotlight: 6f wins at Windsor and Ascot last summer and he's of interest on the latter effort; 33-1 and offered little in a 5f handicap at Newcastle four weeks ago; should be sharper today but others bring more compelling claims.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran excellent second on stable debut at Kempton last time
runners_data.comment: Good 2nd on stable debut last month; up in class but not out of it
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 for his stable debut at Kempton (6f, AW) last month but he ran a cracker for second, beaten a nose; up in grade today but not out of it on last year's turf best.

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 160 days off, prefers 5f trips over this 6f distance
runners_data.comment: Flourished in the second half of 2025 but over 5f; returns from a break off a tough mark
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed a revival in the second half of 2025, winning five 5f handicaps on good ground or slower; no show over 6f when last seen in November and he returns to action off a tough mark.

races.paceDynamic: Montezin is the only confirmed front runner and will lead this field without significant early pressure from 16 runners. Change Sings, Gweedore, Lakers, Cindy Lou Who and Hucklesbrook will track in prominent positions but none are aggressive early pace-setters. The moderate early gallop will allow the large field to stay bunched through halfway, setting up a cavalry charge from the 2f pole. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late kicks, as the sustainable pace will leave plenty in the tank for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate throughout allowing closers full scope
scenarios.body: The bunched field and steady gallop creates perfect conditions for horses with turn of foot to unleash late. Hold-up specialists like Arctic Thunder, Brian, Mirabeau and Brosay get ideal conditions to time their runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses jump Montezin turning for home
scenarios.body: Change Sings, Lakers or Cindy Lou Who press forward from their tracking positions to strike in the final 1.5f. Their race fitness and tactical positioning proves decisive over the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Montezin Wires All
scenarios.trigger: If Montezin maintains his lead and the pace stays too slow for closers
scenarios.body: The front runner gets soft fractions and has enough left to repel all challenges in the final furlong. His recent AW form translates well to this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Specialist Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine 5f-6f specialists find extra gears late
scenarios.body: Juan Les Pins or Wheels Of Fire use their sprint speed to cut through the field in a fast finish. Their recent wins at shorter trips give them the raw pace needed.

watchPoints.text: Montezin could steal this if he gets completely uncontested fractions and the field fails to organize a challenge
Arctic Thunder's 185-day layoff is a concern despite his class advantage and ideal race setup
Juan Les Pins carries just 116lbs and has winning momentum from his last two starts
Several hold-up horses like Addison Grey and Brian are returning from long breaks or poor recent form
The good ground conditions suit most runners with only minor going concerns in this large field
